description.narrative: Access to electricity in Syria has been severely affected by 14 years of conflict. Electricity generation capacity dropped from 8,500MW in 2010, to 5,800 MW in 2011 and to 1,700 MW in 2025 due to severe damage sustained to major power plants and lack of infrastructure maintenance. Since 2020, recurrent fuel shortages and soaring fuel prices have further strained the country’s fossil-fuel-dependent energy system. Furthermore, a lack of public budget and an inability to import essential spare parts, largely due to the constraints of sanctions, have severely limited efforts to rehabilitate damaged electricity generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure, as well as to maintain existing facilities. Damage to transmission and distribution networks has, in many cases, led to generation facilities being disconnected from the grid.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
